The cost of producing distributed and large-scale battery packs in the United States is higher than the global average cost of production, in large part because the supply chain is mostly located in China, which means higher shipping costs and Section 301 tariffs for the relevant materials, parts, and manufacturing equipment shipped to the United States from China. Additionally, final products incur 3–5 times higher U.S. labor costs to assemble domestically. Discussion PV supply chain growth has resulted in U.S. jobs and U.S.-produced PV products used within domestic installations—we estimate 13,260 manufacturing jobs in 2024 across segments of the PV and BESS supply chains. This figure is less than the 33,300 solar manufacturing jobs reported by the Interstate Renewable Energy Council (IREC) National Solar Jobs Census in 2023. We do not estimate manufacturing jobs for several areas of the supply chain—including many structural and electrical elements—and the IREC manufacturing jobs total includes some equipment sales and delivery roles plus other positions not included in our estimates. Much of the growth in domestic production capacity utilized various tax credits available for U.S. manufacturers in 2024. We estimate the PV and BESS supply chains absorbed $3.2 billion in 45X tax credits in 2024 (Figure ES-3). However, this estimate relies on several assumptions, including full production at some new facilities, which we believe were still ramping during 2024, and the omission of some products whose production is wholly unknown. 3 Most of the domestic battery cells produced in 2024 used lithium/nickel/manganese/cobalt (NMC) chemistry, while 2024 BESS products were mostly designed to use lithium/iron (Fe)/phosphate (LFP) cells. Additionally, while most battery cells produced for non-BESS use (e.g., for electric vehicle applications) are very similar in specifications to those used for BESS, there are typically minor differences made during the manufacturing process. Manufacturing lines can usually be altered for either application, but domestic battery cell manufacturers used their lines for existing orders for non-BESS applications. 4 We use a conversion factor of 1,034 t/GWh for anode materials and 2,202 t/GWh for cathode materials (Gohlke et al. 2024).
